model.intended_use: Pretrained generative text model intended as a base for commercial and research use in English and other supported languages; developers can build assistant-like chat applications, natural language generation tasks, or further fine-tune it for other purposes.
limitations: not instruction-tuned out of the box
may produce inaccurate, biased, or objectionable outputs
primarily trained and tested in English; performance in other supported languages may vary
knowledge limited to pretraining data cutoff (Dec 2023)

references.title: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model card (contains base-model benchmark table and family documentation)
config.json mirror (unsloth/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B) used to verify architecture fields for the gated meta-llama repo

provenance.notes: Meta discloses pretraining stages (initial pre-training, long-context continued pre-training, annealing) and high-level data-processing steps, corpus scale (~15T tokens), and cutoff (Dec 2023), but does not release an exact dataset inventory or mixture ratios.

transformation.objective: Train a dense decoder-only Transformer foundation model on a large multilingual/code/math text corpus for general-purpose next-token prediction, later extended to 128K context via continued pretraining.
transformation.notes: Exact compute budget, optimizer settings, and full dataset mixture ratios are not disclosed in the model card or paper excerpt reviewed; the paper (arXiv 2407.21783) describes methodology at a high level (data curation, scaling laws, infrastructure) without a fully itemized dataset list.

datasets.name: Llama 3.1 pretraining data mixture
datasets.description: A new mix of publicly available online data (~15 trillion multilingual tokens), covering general web text, code, math, and multilingual content, processed through deduplication, HTML extraction/cleaning, quality filtering, PII- and unsafe/adult-domain filtering, and domain-specific code/math and multilingual processing.

safety.risk_level: Meta describes a multi-faceted safety process (data curation, red-teaming for CBRNE/child-safety/cyber-risk, refusal-tone tuning) applied across the Llama 3.1 family; the base model itself carries a broad disclaimer of warranty and liability and is not safety fine-tuned (no RLHF/DPO alignment applied to this checkpoint).

items.description: As a pretrained-only checkpoint (no instruction/safety tuning), outputs may be inaccurate, biased, unsafe or objectionable if used directly in user-facing applications.
Meta recommends deploying system-level safeguards (e.g., Llama Guard 3, Prompt Guard, Code Shield) around Llama Materials in production/agentic use.
Use must comply with the Llama 3.1 Acceptable Use Policy, which prohibits illegal activity, generation of CSAM, weapons development (incl. CBRNE), and other listed disallowed uses.

licenses.name: Llama 3.1 Community License Agreement
restrictions: Licensees (or affiliates) with >700 million monthly active users in the preceding calendar month must request a separate license from Meta
Must prominently display 'Built with Llama' on related website/UI/blogpost/about page/product documentation
Any derivative AI model distributed must include 'Llama' at the beginning of its name
Must retain a 'Notice' text file attribution: 'Llama 3.1 is licensed under the Llama 3.1 Community License, Copyright (c) Meta Platforms, Inc. All Rights Reserved.'
Must comply with the Acceptable Use Policy (prohibits illegal, CSAM, CBRNE-weapons-development, and other listed uses)
